transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-01
Time: 14:00 - 14:46 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (AuroraCloud - Partner PM), Samir Khatri (AuroraCloud - Integration Lead), Maya Rodriguez (AuroraCloud - Marketplace Ops)

Summary: Quick technical sync to align on steps to publish Redwood as a marketplace listing inside AuroraCloud's marketplace, review reference architecture for private deployments (VPC option), and outline the joint solution doc and pilot. Covered listing metadata, authentication/KMS flow, network/topology, onboarding sandbox tests, and next steps for a joint PRD.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everybody, thanks for joining, um, appreciate you making time. Alex from Redwood here, AE on the deal. We got Priya from the SE team. Jordan, Samir, Maya, you there on the AuroraCloud side?
[00:18] Jordan Lee: Yeah hi, Jordan here. Thanks Alex, yep, ready.
[00:22] Samir Khatri: Samir here.
[00:25] Maya Rodriguez: And Maya, thanks.
[00:27] Priya Patel: Cool. Quick agenda: marketplace listing checklist, reference architecture for private / VPC deployment, joint solution collateral and pilot timeline, and any blockers e.g., compliance or logos.
[00:40] Jordan Lee: Sounds good. Our product ops wants to know differences between Redwood hosted listing vs dedicated/on-prem bundle we surface in the marketplace. Also need minimal security docs for the listing page.
[00:52] Alex Kim: Absolutely. For the marketplace listing we usually provide: product description, short and long, pricing tier notes (hosted API vs Redwood Dedicated), required permissions, support contact, logos, and links to security docs (SOC2, ISO, SAML docs). We'll share a checklist.
[01:15] Samir Khatri: One thing — for private deployments we need a clear reference arch showing VPC peering, KMS integration for customer keys, and how audit logs flow back to AuroraCloud.
[01:30] Priya Patel: Yep, we can draft that. Our private product exposes a customer-managed control plane that talks to the runtime over mutual TLS, and we have KMS integrations with AWS KMS and customer HSMs. We'll include a flow diagram. Note: sometimes the transcript auto says K V cash instead of KV cache, so sorry for any confusion, but it's the KV cache we use for chat state.
[01:52] Jordan Lee: Ha, yeah. The ops team will want to see the sequence for key rotation and proof of encryption in transit at rest.
[02:05] Alex Kim: We can include rotation docs — we have an integration pattern: customer KMS -> Redwood control plane (encrypted) -> GPU hosts never see plaintext. We will include an appendix with log snippets and sample audit event formats.
[02:25] Maya Rodriguez: For the listing metadata, we have a template: short blurb 150 chars, long blurb 500-800 chars, screenshots, support url, pricing model field and a certified partner checkbox. We'll need the final copy and at least one screenshot of the console.
[02:45] Priya Patel: We can provide a console screenshot and the short/long copy. Also, do you want a pre-built reference architecture diagram in Lucid or draw.io format?
[02:58] Jordan Lee: Lucid preferred, but draw.io is fine.
[03:05] Samir Khatri: On the technical side, curious about network egress — does Redwood prefer to deploy in a VPC within the customer account or do you support a managed VPC from Redwood side for marketplace installs?
[03:18] Priya Patel: Good question. We support both: a) customer-owned VPC where Redwood runtime is deployed as a managed appliance with control plane in Redwood cloud (private control plane option), and b) fully hosted in Redwood cloud (hosted listing). For marketplace 'private' offering we usually recommend customer-deployed private package (our marketplace listing can include an AMI/helm chart or 1-click deploy). We'll document the tradeoffs (latency, support, updates).
[03:46] Jordan Lee: Ok, ops likes the 1-click, but they worry about upgrades. How do we do canary/rollout with marketplace installs?
[03:55] Priya Patel: We include a rollout plan: version pinning via config, canary nodes, and the ability to opt in to auto-upgrades. We'll share the rollout doc.
[04:06] Jordan Lee: Great.
[04:10] [04:10] Speaker 2 (Samir): Um, we also need to make sure the onboarding terraform module matches the networking constraints — we have strict NACLs and need to know port lists.
[04:22] Priya Patel: We'll provide the ports list. Generally it's 443 for control plane, grpc/8443 for runtime comms internally, and ssh for ops if you enable it. We'll send a security checklist.
[04:36] Alex Kim: I'll attach a spreadsheet with the port list and recommended NACL examples.
[04:42] Jordan Lee: Perfect.
[04:45] [04:45] Maya Rodriguez: Regarding security docs for the listing, would a short SOC2 statement plus a link to full PDF suffice? We also have an internal cert page that lists encryption, SSO, etc.
[04:56] Alex Kim: Yes, short summary plus link is ideal. We'll include SAML/SSO and SCIM capabilities, RBAC, and audit logs examples.
[05:06] Priya Patel: On the KMS side — do you require HSM attestation and FIPS endpoints?
[05:12] Jordan Lee: For some enterprise customers yes — but marketplace listing doesn't need that on the page, just a note 'supports customer-managed KMS and HSM' and then detailed docs in the partner portal.
[05:26] Samir Khatri: Also, how about billing integration — do you want usage metering sent to AuroraCloud for consolidated billing?
[05:34] Alex Kim: We support two models: partner-billing via marketplace (AuroraCloud charges customers) or direct billing (Redwood bills). For partner-billing we emit a usage fileDaily/weekly via S3 + signed manifest or a push callback webhook. We'll include the format in the listing appendix.
[05:52] Jordan Lee: Good, ops will verify the S3 flow with their billing team.
[05:56] [05:56] Speaker 1 (Priya): One technical note: when we talk about caching — prefix/KV caching — sometimes the transcript says K V cash, but it's KV cache which affects token spend. We'll include quantization and batch sizing recommendations for AuroraCloud workloads.
[06:16] Samir Khatri: On performance: do you have verified profiles for common models? We need latency and throughput numbers for our reference arch doc.
[06:25] Priya Patel: Yes, we maintain a model catalog with performance profiles across instance types. We'll attach a couple of benchmark CSVs (p95 latency for seq len 128/512, throughput with batching). Note that these are approximate; we'll recommend you run a short smoke test in your sandbox to validate.
[06:45] Jordan Lee: Let's plan for that. Can we get a sample test harness?
[06:49] Alex Kim: We'll share a simple k6/journey script and a small prompt set.
[06:53] Jordan Lee: Thanks.
[06:55] [06:55] Maya Rodriguez: For the joint solution doc, our marketing requires a one-pager: value props, architecture diagram, customer persona, and a 'how to get started' steps. We'll need that to do co-marketing.
[07:10] Alex Kim: We'll draft the one-pager. Priya can own the technical portion.
[07:16] Priya Patel: I'll take the reference arch and the integration steps.
[07:20] Jordan Lee: On certification: AuroraCloud has a 'featured' badge for partners who pass a checklist (security, support response time, etc). What is Redwood's standard SLA for Dedicated / Private installs?
[07:32] Alex Kim: Dedicated has SLA tiers; for private installs we offer enterprise support packages with a 99.9% target and optional dedicated support. We'll include an SLA summary for each deployment mode.
[07:45] Samir Khatri: Any known blockers around data residency? We have EEA customers who require logs to stay in-region.
[07:53] Priya Patel: We support region pinning and can keep audit logs in your region via S3/stack. We'll document options.
[08:02] Jordan Lee: Awesome.
[08:05] [08:05] Speaker 3 (Jordan): Quick Q on listing screenshots: do you have a sanitized screenshot of the Console that shows creation of an inference endpoint without PII?
[08:15] Alex Kim: Yes, we can produce sanitized images. We'll provide 3 sizes: banner, thumbnail, and detailed console shot.
[08:22] Maya Rodriguez: For marketplace review, we need app icons in SVG and PNG 512x512.
[08:27] Alex Kim: Noted. We'll attach the assets.
[08:30] Priya Patel: Back to the reference arch — we'll show two flows: 1) Marketplace hosted Redwood - traffic proxied via AuroraCloud, 2) Customer-deployed - VPC + control plane interactions. We'll include ports, key flows, and a note about canary rollouts.
[08:47] Samir Khatri: For the customer-deployed option, can we see a terraform module?
[08:51] Priya Patel: We have an example terraform module and helm chart in our partner repo; we'll share a link and strip any internal stuff.
[08:59] Jordan Lee: If we want to list a 'joint solution' product, what are the acceptance criteria?
[09:06] Alex Kim: Typically: documented integration, security checklist passed, sample deployment validated in your sandbox, co-marketing one-pager, and legal/merchant terms agreed. We'll work with your partner ops team on exact gating.
[09:22] Maya Rodriguez: That works.
[09:25] [09:25] Speaker 2 (Samir): A random nit: in the runtime, what's your approach to model fallbacks? If a pinned model is unavailable do you fallback to a smaller variant?
[09:36] Priya Patel: Yes, smart routing supports fallback to compatible variants by policy (latency vs cost). We can show sample config for fallback policies.
[09:45] Jordan Lee: Good to know.
[09:48] [09:48] Alex Kim: Ok, let's capture concrete deliverables: we'll share marketplace checklist, sandbox test scripts, reference arch draft, and the pricing/billing integration spec. Samir will provide sandbox creds. Maya will confirm marketing asset requirements.
[10:04] Samir Khatri: I'll get the sandbox and a minimal test dataset to you by EOD Nov 4.
[10:12] Maya Rodriguez: I'll provide the marketplace template and exact icon specs by Nov 5.
[10:18] Alex Kim: Priya — can you draft the reference arch by Nov 6?
[10:21] Priya Patel: Yep.
[10:24] [10:24] Jordan Lee: We'll schedule a follow-up review on Nov 8 to walk the doc and sign off. 
[10:31] Alex Kim: Sounds good. Anything else?
[10:34] [10:34] Maya Rodriguez: One last question — for billing, do you have the usage file schema?
[10:40] Alex Kim: Yes, CSV with columns: customer_id, timestamp, tokens_in, tokens_out, model_id, usage_units. We'll include sample and webhook payload.
[10:48] Jordan Lee: Perfect.
[10:50] [10:50] Speaker 1 (Priya): We'll also note that there may be small transcription issues in these notes — e.g., KV cache sometimes transcribed funny.
[10:59] Alex Kim: Great. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the checklist and the draft docs.
[11:05] Jordan Lee: Thanks all. Talk soon.

Recap / Explicit next steps (verbal):
- Redwood: share marketplace listing checklist, security docs, sanitized screenshots, sample benchmark CSV, and test harness (k6) by 2026-11-03 to 2026-11-06 window.
- AuroraCloud: provide sandbox account and test data by 2026-11-04, confirm icon/logo specs by 2026-11-05.
- Both: review reference architecture draft on 2026-11-08 meeting.

References mentioned (links to be shared after):
- Partner repo sample terraform/helm chart (will share link)
- Benchmark CSVs (p95 latency, throughput)
- Marketplace listing template (AuroraCloud portal)

End of transcript.
